evals.name: overbuilt-small-project
evals.prompt: Review this proposal for our small one-instance photo app: split it into 12 microservices, add a service mesh, event bus, CQRS, and a separate database per service. The only stated requirement is to let two developers ship faster.
evals.expected_output: Flags disproportionate complexity, missing evidence, operational costs, and lack of goals/non-goals; recommends a simpler modular monolith or asks for scaling/ownership evidence.
assertions: The review connects the proposed complexity to the actual one-instance/two-developer context
At least one concrete operational or failure cost is cited
The recommendation is one simpler path rather than an equal menu

evals.name: api-design-missing-rollback
evals.prompt: Review this design: rename the public `email` field to `contact` in the next release and update all clients later. There is no compatibility window or rollback plan.
evals.expected_output: Reports a high-confidence breaking contract finding, explains affected clients, and recommends an additive expand/migrate/contract path or versioned transition with tests.
assertions: The breaking public contract is reported with high severity
The recommendation includes a compatibility or migration path
The review asks how rollback and old clients are handled

evals.name: good-design-no-false-positives
evals.prompt: Review this design for a three-person app: keep one deployable, split code by business capability, each module owns its tables, HTTP handlers call use cases, and an integration test verifies the checkout flow. Goals and non-goals are listed; alternatives are documented.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent blockers; acknowledges strengths and reports no blocking findings or only evidence-based questions.
assertions: The review does not call modularity or one deployable an architectural flaw without evidence
The report acknowledges explicit goals, alternatives, and integration coverage
The verdict is approve or approve with changes, not reject
